sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are uniform across the five active books (`exit_confirm_screens`: 2, `reentry_cooldown_screens`: 1, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp`: 10.0), but the 7d panel shows they are not binding: every track has `buffered_holdings`: 0, empty `exit_streak` and `reentry_cooldown`, `adjacent_flip_count`: 0, and no `duplicate_day_skip` on the latest pass. Recent activity is subdued on control and DCA twins (`buy_tier_level` 0 trades in 7d; `buy_tier_level_dca` 4), while primary `ai_judgment_fair` still carries the watch alert at lifetime `cost_drag` 0.1459 and `trade_count` 49 despite only 2 trades in 7d. Epoch-scoped primary economics look materially better (`learning_track_epoch_datum` epoch `cost_drag` implied via epoch costs: epoch block shows `cost_drag` 0.0282 on `post_apply_trade_count` 39 with `benchmark_span_available`: true), and the 7d buffered-hold replay on primary shows `cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher` 0.0 with `trade_count_delta_lower_minus_higher` 1 (screens=1 adds one trade, not less drag). The single biggest operational learning gap is reconciling primary lifetime churn (`total_costs` 145.93, 14.6% drag) with guard state and thin log replay (4 `log_entries_in_window`, L111 pre-logging gap): matched-30 twins run the same guard stack at ~0.008–0.010 `cost_drag`, so construction/rotation history—not hold-buffer occupancy—dominates the primary alert.
